_comment: Per-agent capabilities. Adding an agent is a one-line change here, never a code path. Capabilities: `interruptKey` the bytes that stop a running turn (null: none); `resume` how a session is resumed (`flag` or `subcommand`) with `resumeArg` its argument; `sessionId` whether QualityLayer `chosen` the id before the start or `discovered` it afterwards; `worktreeFlag` the argument that starts in a worktree (null: none); `goal` whether a launch prefixes `/goal`; `permissionModes` the agent's permission modes in the order the footer lists them, each with its `id`, `label`, launch `args` and `level` (`own`, `fewer` or `bypass`: the level the workflow default and the protected-setting check use; a run's `perm` picks the first mode of its level when no mode id is given; no flag at all is the agent's own setting, a mode with no `args` is the same setting by name; the agent's own setting is the `own` mode with no `args`, else the first mode, and no label says so); `permissionSource` where that own setting comes from, named in the footer's default row (null: none); `turnEndHooks` the hook events that end a turn; `promptDelivery` `argument` when the first prompt goes on the command line, behind `promptFlag` when that is set; `managedArgs` what a managed start adds; `conversation` true when the agent writes a session record the Conversation can read (false: Terminal only); `conversationMissing` what that record does not give the Conversation, from `thinking`, `tools`, `results` (tool output), `usage` (tokens and price), `context` (how full the context is) and `approvals`, so the view says what is missing (absent: nothing); `effort` `separate` (its own control), `in-model` (part of the model id) or null (none); `efforts` the levels a session may be set to, lowest first (empty unless `effort` is `separate`); `limits` where its plan limits come from (`session-record`: the `rate_limits` its session record carries; `usage-command`: what the agent's own headless `/usage` prints, and the rows its session record gets when a limit stops it; null: not reported); `account` how the agent's sign-in is read: `command` the arguments of one of its own read-only status commands (never a prompt or a model turn), `reads` the reader in `account-readers.ts` that turns its output into signed in, signed out or unknown, with the plan or provider count when the output names one, and `startedFile` the agent's own settings file when that command writes it on a first run: it is not asked until that file exists (looked up by existence only, never read), in the agent's config folder when the environment moves it (`configDirEnv`), else in the home folder (null: it is asked at once); `modelIds` `listed` when only the models below are offered and `native` when any model id the agent accepts is; `configDirEnv` the variable that moves the agent's folder (null: none); `picker` true when the agent has a question picker the workflow can fill (false: a numbered question in the chat); `modelFlag` the argument that names the model; `effortArgs` the arguments that set the effort, `{effort}` standing for the level (null: none, as when `effort` is `in-model`); `addDirFlag` the argument that grants one more folder (null: none); `worktreeName` how a new worktree's name follows `worktreeFlag`: `separate` as the next argument, `attached` after an equals sign so it never takes the prompt (null: the flag takes none); `trustArgs` what a managed start adds so the agent does not stop at its trust question; `startSession` how a managed start gives a session id QualityLayer chose: `flag` with the `id` it takes (`uuid`, `native`: any id the agent takes and QualityLayer makes as a UUID, or `ses_hex`), or `create`, a subcommand that prints a new id, which the start then resumes (null: the agent picks its own id, found from its first hook or its record); `sessionEnv` the variable a managed start sets so commands the agent runs can name the session when the agent sets none; `identityEnv` the variables that name the agent when one is set in the commands and hooks it runs (Cursor's agent terminal sets `CURSOR_AGENT` and `CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID`, not the hooks' `CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR`); `sessionIdEnv` the variables that hold the agent's own session id there, the first one set wins (the conversation id is the session Cursor and Antigravity record under); `turnRecord` the format of the agent's own record that shows a turn ended when its hook did not run (null: the hooks are enough); `review` how an independent review or second opinion starts this agent headless and read-only, for an agent whose command line is data (absent: `reviewCommand` in `core/review/cross.ts` builds it, and the agent's own flags enforce read-only): `args` the fixed arguments that make the run headless, streaming and read-only (the model, effort and picture folders follow from `modelFlag`, `effortArgs` and `addDirFlag`), `promptFile` the argument that takes the path of a file holding the brief (null: the brief goes on stdin), `promptArg` (optional, with `promptFile` null) the flag whose value is the brief itself, put after the other arguments so a multi-value flag before it ends (Copilot's `-p`; absent: stdin), `readOnly` `enforced` when the agent itself refuses every edit in this run and `detected` when it does not, so the automatic choice of reviewer (Other model family) prefers another maker's model, then an enforced agent, and falls to a detected one only when nothing else qualifies (and a detected agent never works in the person's tree: it reviews a disposable copy of exactly what is reviewed, deleted afterwards), `allowedTools` the tools a review may start, checked on every line of the stream (any other tool start, a stream that does not begin with its init event, or an Antigravity init in another permission mode stops the run at once and fails the review), `trust` whether the run adds `trustArgs` because a headless run refuses an untrusted folder (a trusted folder's project hooks may run during the review, as they do for Claude Code's `-p`), and `note` what the agent is told after the brief about what this review does not let it do (Cursor runs in Plan mode, whose tools refuse a code file but not a markdown one, and Ask mode is not enforced in a headless run; Grok is given only its read tools, every MCP tool is denied, and it never asks; Antigravity has no read-only mode, so it runs in its default one in its sandbox, where a headless run cannot ask and refuses every edit and command). `qualifiedVersion` is the version the agent was last checked with. `goal` is the agent's native keep-going mode, null when it has none; the Implement stop only mentions that it exists. `invoke` is the skill command the user types (`/ql implement <task>`). `helperModels` are the models a fresh-context helper or a review may run on, the first the default, whatever the agent's own model list says; absent leaves it to the agent. `build` is the model advice for the Implement session the user starts, which cuts the Plan into cards and builds them itself and may start subagents: `models` the models it and its subagents may run on, the recommended one for a full task first; `orchestrator` the recommended model of the build session for a full task, chosen from `orchestrators` (listed most capable first); `small` the id of the model recommended for a small change (absent: the `orchestrator`); `subagentModel` true when the build card can set the model the session's subagents run on (absent: the agent chooses its own helpers, and the card says so). `plan` is the same for the Plan: `model` the recommended one of `models`. `modelOrder` is the order every picker lists the agent's models in, by name or family (a provider prefix is ignored; a model it does not name goes last), whatever order the lists above keep for their defaults. `modelCost` ranks the same names by price, so a menu notes each model against the one marked Default (`costs more`, `costs less`); `modelNotes` words a model's note when it costs more than the Default and has a better one to say.
